natural_body: SMB 40% discounts lifted acquisition and near-term revenue but cut retention 12%.

first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory 86 and 31 showed that shortening onboarding and simplifying signup produce durable lifts in activation and completion. These are the most directly causally relevant to the current decline. Verifying these two will confirm whether the conditions under which they succeeded still hold. Memory 91 (activation messaging) is a secondary lever that could compound gains if onboarding improvements unlock more users to receive in-product messaging. Promotional_pricing is rejected because memory 73 showed discounting cuts retention 12%, harming long-term qualified revenue despite short-term acquisition gains—directly contrary to the primary objective. Referral_incentives work for established customers (memory 57), but the current problem is early-stage activation and completion, not scaling existing cohorts. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory 44) is viable but requires different targeting and would not address the SMB price pressure or activation decline. Simplify_onboarding targets the root lever most tightly coupled to both observed declines and prior positive evidence.
